sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Fulton County, New York?
sections.html:
Town collectors take current county and town tax early in the year, and the Fulton County Treasurer takes over anything left unpaid. The Treasurer's office is in the County Office Building at 223 West Main Street, Room 202, Johnstown, NY 12095, phone (518) 736-5580. Its hours are Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, shortened to 4 pm from July 1 through Labor Day.

Per the county's own description, the Treasurer collects delinquent school, village, town and county taxes, runs the foreclosure and auction process under the state Real Property Tax Law, and works with the town tax collectors. It also collects and enforces taxes on parcels in the City of Gloversville, and the page says it does not collect City of Johnstown taxes.

The Real Property Tax Service Agency, at (518) 736-5507 in the same building, was created under Article 15-A of the state Real Property Tax Law in 1970 and maintains the tax maps. Its online Beacon map shows ownership, property inventory and assessed value, refreshed nightly, and explains the parcel's SBL (section, block, lot) number that appears on tax bills and assessment rolls.

sections.h2: What is the Fulton County tax calendar?
sections.html:
Each tax has its own window, and the Treasurer's payments page spells them out. The county and town windows are early in the year, school and village windows come in the fall, and the City of Gloversville has its own calendar.

Fulton County payment windows (source: Fulton County Treasurer payments page)
TaxPay toWindow
County and townTown collectorJanuary 1 to March 31
Unpaid county and townCounty TreasurerReturned April 1, collections begin May 1
VillageVillage collectorJune 1 to October 31
School (town districts)School tax collectorSeptember 1 to October 31
City of GloversvilleCity, then TreasurerApril 1 to October 31, Treasurer from December 1

Village and school payments are not accepted after October 31, and unpaid town school and village amounts are relevied on the next county bill. Current county tax cannot be paid during the first two weeks of April while the books transfer, so call the Treasurer in the last week of April for the amount due. The Treasurer's office takes online payments for delinquent town tax at the end of April, and mailed payments go to P.O. Box 128, Johnstown, NY 12095, never as cash.

sections.h2: Can I pay delinquent Fulton County taxes in installments?
sections.html:
Possibly, but only in May. Local Law No. 2 of 1997 lets the Treasurer sign installment agreements with owners of residential real property, and the county processes them only from May 1 through May 31. Letters go out in April to qualified owners who are behind.

  • The down payment is 25% of the eligible delinquent taxes.
  • Payments are monthly, and the term cannot exceed 24 months.
  • For the May 2026 window, eligible taxes were 2025 county, 2024 school and 2024 city.
  • Commercial property and land are not eligible.
  • A parcel foreclosed on within the last three years, or one that defaulted on an installment agreement in the last three years, is not eligible.

The county page directs owners to call the Treasurer to confirm whether they qualify. The May 2026 window has closed, so the next chance is May 2027.

sections.h2: What happened in the latest Fulton County in rem foreclosure?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's In Rem Foreclosure Properties page set November 30, 2025 as the last day to redeem for parcels with unpaid 2020 school, 2020 City and 2021 County taxes. That date has passed. The page said all taxes had to be paid in full in reverse chronological order by year, with guaranteed funds, and told owners to request a Parcel Status Report from the Treasurer to learn the exact amount owed.

Owners could pay at the Treasurer's office or by card online. The page also pointed people toward the New York State Homeowner Assistance Fund for help with delinquent taxes. The Treasurer's office also handles the foreclosure and auction steps, so anyone with a lien that old should call (518) 736-5580 or email fctreasurer@fultoncountyny.gov before listing a house.

sections.h2: What is Fulton County like for homeowners?
sections.html:
Fulton County is in the Mohawk Valley, with Johnstown as the county seat and Gloversville as the largest city. It was formed on April 18, 1838, from part of Montgomery County. About 58% of its 533 square miles lies inside Adirondack Park. Gloves and leather were the main industry for generations, and few glovers and tanners remain today.

Hamilton County is to the north, Saratoga to the east, Montgomery to the south and Herkimer to the west. State routes 10, 29, 30 and 67 are among the main roads. School districts include Gloversville City, Johnstown City, Broadalbin-Perth, Mayfield, Northville and Galway, and Fulton-Montgomery Community College is in Johnstown. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page gives the housing picture.

The old Tryon County courthouse of 1772 in Johnstown is now the Fulton County Courthouse and is described as New York's oldest operating courthouse. Population has slipped from 55,531 in 2010 to an estimated 52,216 in 2025, and only 85 building permits were recorded in 2025, which is a small number for a county with more than 28,000 housing units. The county's parcel records, searchable through the Beacon map, are the place to check ownership, inventory and assessed value for any house before it is listed.

sections.h2: How do I clear Fulton County tax before closing a sale?
sections.html:
Ask the right office for the right year. The Real Property Tax Service Agency says that during tax collection dates you contact the local tax collector, and outside those dates you contact the County Treasurer for county and town taxes and the city or school collector for those taxes.

  1. Find the parcel's SBL number on the Beacon map or the tax bill.
  2. Call the Treasurer at (518) 736-5580 and ask for a Parcel Status Report on any delinquent year.
  3. Pay older years first, since the Treasurer requires reverse chronological order for foreclosure redemption.
  4. Ask about exemptions, STAR and veteran or senior benefits through your assessor or the county's real property office at (518) 736-5509. STAR applications go to the state directly.
  5. Give the closing attorney the written payoff amounts.

The Treasurer's office can say which taxing districts are involved when a parcel straddles city, town and school bills.

faqs.q: When can I pay Fulton County tax to my town collector?
faqs.a: January 1 through March 31. After that the town collector returns unpaid bills to the County Treasurer, and the Treasurer's office begins collections on May 1.

faqs.q: Is there a Fulton County installment plan for back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, for eligible owners of residential property, but agreements are processed only in May. The down payment is 25% of the eligible delinquent tax, the term is up to 24 months, and payments are monthly.

faqs.q: Does the Fulton County Treasurer collect City of Johnstown taxes?
faqs.a: No. The Treasurer's page says it does not collect City of Johnstown taxes, though it does collect City of Gloversville parcels. For Johnstown, contact the city.

faqs.q: How do I find a Fulton County parcel's tax map number?
faqs.a: Use the Beacon online map from the Real Property Tax Service Agency. It shows the SBL, also called the tax map number, along with ownership and assessed value. The same number appears on tax bills and assessment rolls.

faqs.q: How do I apply for STAR in Fulton County?
faqs.a: Apply directly with New York State. The Real Property Tax Service Agency's page says owners now register with the state, and gives (518) 457-2036 as the state number.
